messages:
Lia: heads-up — after last week's kernel-selection change i see a 95th+ tail increase on the gpt-ish family when prefix cache hit rate > 60%
Dan: can you paste the flame/profile? wondering if it's kernel_launch overhead or just smaller batches causing worse GPU utilization
Lia: short dump from pprof: 
```
CPU: kernel_launch_overhead ~ 42% of host-side time
GPU occupancy fine for bulk calls, but avg batch size drops from 18->6 when cache hits high
queue_wait reduced but tx overhead up
```
Priya: that smells like fragmentation: cache hits produce short-token requests that avoid kv recompute, so batching groups are shorter and we end up switching kernels more often (quantized vs fp16 paths)
Max: we changed selection to prefer the lower-latency kernel for short sequences — that decision has a ~1.2ms kernel_dispatch penalty per switch vs keeping batched larger kernel. If batches shrink we pay more switches per token
Sean: timeline: kernel selector commit r1234 rolled 2 days ago? InfraBot: deploy-bot: rolled r1234 to canary at 2026-11-03T09:12:22Z -> prod 2026-11-04T02:04:10Z :shipit:
Lia: yes.^ that matches timing. How much of tail is from pure dispatch vs serialization / memcpy?
Dan: from traces it's ~65% dispatch/driver latency, memcpy smaller. So driver/kernel churn is dominant.
Priya: proposed quick experiments: 
- bump continuous-batcher token_budget target from 1024 -> 1536 (gives more room to merge short jobs)
- add cache-hit-aware packing: prefer packers that combine hit+miss if combined token sum < thresh
- introduce 200us scheduling delay for cache-hit-only queues to accumulate more requests
Lia: +1 to experiments. note: delaying might affect p99 for ultra-low-latency customers — need per-tenant policy
Max: alternative: keep kernel selector conservative: prefer single-kernel path for mixed batches (avoid switch). cheap config flip. Could be lowest-risk rollback to previous selector until we have packer changes
Sean: can we simulate with our replay harness? Lia: yes — i'll run replay with high prefix-hit traces (from prod/metrics/prefix-cache/hot_top_10) and compare p50/p95/p99 for three knobs: token_budget, scheduling_delay, kernel_pref
Dan: also capture kernel_launch_count metric per-second and avg_batch_size distribution. Those are good signals for 'fragmentation'
Priya: code snippets for packer heuristic I sketched: 
```
// pseudo
if (batch.has_miss && incoming.is_cache_hit) {
  if (batch.token_sum + incoming.tokens <= HIT_MIX_THRESHOLD) {
    packTogether(); // avoid leaving small isolated hit batches
  }
}
```
Lia: any other gotchas? model-specific kernel affinity? Some architectures prefer quant path even for mixed sequences -> could regress quality. Need canary with evals
Max: +1 on evals; i'll add a fast quality check set and block rollout if model perplexity shifts > 0.8%
Sean: action items: Lia run replay experiments and drop results here; Max add QA eval gating; Dan add kernel_launch_count & avg_batch_size dashboards; Priya prepare packer PR (small, feature-flagged).
Lia: i'll run replays now, will post perf table in ~30m. thanks all :party_parrot:
